newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysia opposition MP appeals sedition conviction.
newsitem.headline: Malaysia opposition MP appeals sedition conviction.

text.p: A Malaysian opposition lawmaker appealed against his conviction for sedition on Friday and said he would sue if an election was held prematurely for the parliamentary seat he stands to lose.

Lim Guan Eng, deputy secretary-general of the Democratic Action Party (DAP), said he was the rightful member of parliament (MP) for the Kota Melaka district in southwestern Malacca state until the court ruled on his appeal.
"I wish to warn...that I will sue the Election Commission should they take any steps to declare the Kota Melaka parliamentary seat vacant and hold a by-election immediately," he said in a statement.
He was reacting to press reports quoting Election Commission chairman Harun Din on Wednesday as saying that "preparations" were being made to hold a contest for the seat.

Lim was convicted on April 28 for publishing a pamphlet entitled "Ceramah Kisah Benar" (The True Story), which prosecutors said contained false information on a sex scandal involving a schoolgirl and former chief minister of Malacca.
Lim had said in the pamphlet that authorities made the schoolgirl an "imprisoned victim" when the sex scandal broke. That earned him the sedition charge.
He was fined 15,000 ringgit (US$6,000), and will be jailed nine months if he does not pay.
Under Malaysian law an MP can be unseated after receiving a as little as a 2,000 ringgit fine.
Attorney-General Mohtar Abdullah is pressing for a greater punishment when the appeal is heard.
"The attorney-general is clearly asking for a jail sentence," said Lim. "It only proves he abuses his power by practising selective prosecution against DAP MPs." ($1=2.51 ringgit)
